title: Finite-dimensional tangent space of a locally finite type algebraic stack
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and use schemes in the universes of [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] admitting a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$ whose composite $U\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of finite type as an $R$-algebra and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be an $S$-morphism. On the Artinian local test category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category], define $\mathcal F_x(A)$ to have objects $(\eta,\alpha)$ where $\eta\in\mathcal X(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ and $\alpha:\eta|_k\xrightarrow{\sim}x$; arrows are isomorphisms respecting $\alpha$, and transport is pullback. Its tangent space $T_x=\pi_0\mathcal F_x(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$, the set of marked first-order deformations up to isomorphism, with zero the pullback of $x$ along $k\to k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, scalar multiplication by $a\in k$ induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$, and addition defined by lifting two classes to $k[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1^2,\epsilon_1\epsilon_2,\epsilon_2^2)$ and transporting along $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon$ (the lift is unique up to isomorphism), is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. No properness, separatedness, smoothness of $\mathcal X$ over $S$, or restriction on the stabilizers is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), tangent-space assertion, with the marked predeformation category of equation-predeformation-category. Affine Noetherian base specialization.

proof.text: Apply the algebraic-stack Rim--Schlessinger theorem to $\mathcal X$. Its hypotheses require neither local finite type nor any condition on stabilizers. Its conclusion is exactly the pushout property required by the marked-deformation field-extension lemma. That lemma makes $\mathcal F_x$ a predeformation category satisfying (RS), and gives its canonical vector structure, with the zero, addition, and scalar multiplication in the statement. In particular the lift of a pair of tangent classes is unique up to isomorphism: the product comparison is an equivalence of groupoids over the terminal marked fibre at $k$, hence a bijection on isomorphism classes. For every finite extension $l/k$ the same lemma gives $T_x\otimes_k l\simeq T_{x_l}$, with the pullback map $v\mapsto v\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), field-extension reduction; Tags 07WQ (lemma-algebraic-stack-RS), 07WU (lemma-deformation-category), 07WX (lemma-change-of-field), and formal-defos.tex Tag 07WB (lemma-tangent-space-change-of-field).

proof.text: Form $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\mathcal X}U$. By the definition of the given atlas, $Z$ is a nonempty algebraic space smooth and surjective over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to Z$. Then $W$ is nonempty and $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by the chart definition of smoothness for this projection. The dense-separable-points lemma gives a point of $W$ with residue field $l$ finite separable over $k$: a dense subset of a nonempty space is nonempty. Its image in $Z$ is precisely a morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}l\to U$ with a specified isomorphism $p(u)\simeq x_l$. Since $l$ has a finite $k$-basis, adjoining that basis and finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $k$ generates $l$ over $R$. Thus $l$ is an allowed finite-type residue field. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq U$ through $u$ with $B$ a finite type $R$-algebra, using the affine cover in the definition of locally finite type over the affine base.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), first paragraph; Tag 07W4 (spaces-over-fields.tex, lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense), here obtained from a scheme chart and the existing Tag 056U node.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ represent any class of $T_{x_l}$ and put $D=l[\epsilon]$. The atlas definition gives a smooth algebraic space $Z_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}D\times_{\mathcal X}U$ over $\operatorname{Spec}D$. The marking of $\eta$, the chosen $u$, and the isomorphism $p(u)\simeq x_l$ give a section over $\operatorname{Spec}l$. The closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}l\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}D$ is an affine first order thickening, since its ideal $(\epsilon)$ has square zero. Apply the smooth-space affine infinitesimal lifting lemma to this section, with base map the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}D$. Its lift is a morphism $\widetilde u:\operatorname{Spec}D\to U$, reducing to $u$, together with an isomorphism $p(\widetilde u)\simeq\eta$ inducing the prescribed marking. Both spectra have a single point, so $\widetilde u$ factors through $V$. Consequently the natural map from marked tangent lifts of $u$ in $V$ onto $T_{x_l}$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), final paragraph, tangent surjectivity; Tag 07WK (lemma-formally-smooth-on-deformation-categories), here expanded using spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth).

proof.text: Write $\varphi_0:B\to l$ for $u$. A marked tangent lift in $V$ is an $R$-algebra map $\varphi:B\to l[\epsilon]$ reducing to $\varphi_0$; a representable scheme has no nonidentity arrows. There is a unique function $d:B\to l$ with $\varphi(b)=\varphi_0(b)+\epsilon d(b)$. The ring-map equations are exactly $d(b+c)=d(b)+d(c)$, $d(bc)=\varphi_0(b)d(c)+\varphi_0(c)d(b)$ and $d(r)=0$ for $r\in R$. Conversely these equations define such a lift. These functions form an $l$-vector space under pointwise operations. If $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ over $R$, evaluating $d$ on them is an injective linear map into $l^n$: addition and the product rule determine $d$ on every polynomial in the $b_i$, and these polynomials exhaust $B$. Thus the atlas tangent space is finite-dimensional (at most $n$), including $n=0$. This argument uses algebra generators, not generators of $\ker\varphi_0$.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), last affine-coordinate argument and omitted details; corrected to use finite algebra generators in place of generators of the point ideal.

proof.text: The map of step 3 from this vector space to $T_{x_l}$ is linear. Indeed the constant lift maps to the constant stack object, and pullback commutes with each map $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$, giving scalar compatibility. For $d_1,d_2$, the single map $b\mapsto\varphi_0(b)+\epsilon_1d_1(b)+\epsilon_2d_2(b)$ into $l[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2]/(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)^2$ restricts to the two ring lifts. Its image under $p$ therefore represents the unique pair-lift in the definition of stack tangent addition. Transport along $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\mapsto\epsilon$ sends it to the image of $d_1+d_2$. This proves additive compatibility. A finite basis of the atlas tangent space has images spanning $T_{x_l}$ by the surjectivity of step 3. Hence $T_{x_l}$ is finite-dimensional over $l$.

source.place: Tag 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension), final paragraph: linearity and surjectivity; formal-defos.tex Tag 06IJ (lemma-k-linear-differential), here verified directly from the operations.

proof.text: Finally use $T_x\otimes_k l\simeq T_{x_l}$. Choose a finite $k$-basis of $l$ starting with $1$; its first coordinate defines a $k$-linear functional $\lambda:l\to k$ with $\lambda(1)=1$. The map $v\mapsto v\otimes1$ is injective, since $v\otimes a\mapsto\lambda(a)v$ is a left inverse. A finite $l$-spanning set of $T_{x_l}$ multiplied by the finitely many basis elements of $l/k$ spans it over $k$. Its $k$-subspace $T_x$ is therefore finite-dimensional. The vector operations were already identified in step 1, so this proves every clause of the item without adding any smoothness or separation hypothesis on $\mathcal X$.

Sources read: artin.tex 07X1 (lemma-finite-dimension, full proof), 07WQ, 07WU, 07WX and formal-defos.tex 07WB. No SGA anywhere. Source error confirmed: the last paragraph of 07X1 says a lift is determined by its values on generators of the point ideal ker phi0, which is false for an inseparable residue map (R=F_p(s), B=l=R[t]/(t^p-s), phi0=id; t->t+c*epsilon is a lift for every c). Step 4 counts on R-algebra generators of B instead, which is correct. Step checks: (1) the RS node's conclusion is exactly the new node's hypothesis, and the pair-lift is unique by RS on k[e] x_k k[e]. (2) The atlas fibre is smooth over k, so a chart W is smooth by the chartwise definition. The 056U node gives a separable finite point l, which is of finite type over R, and an affine V=Spec B with B finitely generated. (3) The smooth-space affine lifting lemma applies along Spec l in Spec l[e] with b=id. The lift keeps the marking, and it lies in V because Spec l[e] has one point. (4) Lifts are phi0-derivations vanishing on R; evaluation on algebra generators is injective; n=0 and the inseparable case checked. (5) Scalars and zero are direct. Addition: the two-parameter map is the unique pair-lift. So the map is linear and onto. (6) A functional with lambda(1)=1 gives a left inverse of v->v(x)1, so T_x embeds in T_{x_l}, which is finite over k.
